question: Q-f4-learned-topology-causal-contribution
conjecture: With the typed store frozen at checkpoint W* (WANN-style topology/weight separation), the learned topology E_learned does causal work: it beats degree-sequence-preserved shuffle, clique completion, and |E|-matched random sparse topologies on fresh heldout, its edge LOO-importance removal curve dominates random removal (AUC gap > 0), and topology edit distance correlates with heldout delta across learning checkpoints (Spearman rho CI excludes 0).

arms.A: learned topology E_learned (weights frozen at W*)
arms.B: shuffled topology (same degree sequence, same hyperedge count, random rewiring)

secondary_discriminators.edge_ablation_causal_curve: top-k removal by edge LOO importance (k=0..|E|) vs random removal at same k - preregistered AUC gap effect size
secondary_discriminators.structure_performance_correlation: Spearman rho(topology edit distance between checkpoints, heldout delta) + CI

already_public_before_registration.note: C1 book-scale kill is public receipt: clique 0.447 > hswm 0.427 (novel kill) - this gate is its direct follow-up. Literature: structure learning often fails to beat static/random controls (TGB/OpenGSL/G-Designer/DyLAN).
already_public_before_registration.harness_provenance: existing gate harness; no new infra required (finding c4)

kill_conditions: f4_k1 any of B/C/D catches A within CI margin -> topology-learning claim killed (structure does no causal work)
f4_k2 AUC gap CI includes 0 -> flat causal curve killed (AgentPrune-style null reproduction)
f4_k3 rho CI includes 0 -> only the 'learning' part killed; demote to static-structure effect
pass_conditions: edge ablation AUC gap > 0 (prereg effect size)
